thread:
alex-support: FYI, urgent support ticket from TimCorp on Dedicated pool-43. Getting a bunch of 429s and long tails. Customer says autoscale didn’t add nodes.
leah-customer-success: Customer timeline: spikes at 09:05 -> sustained 2k rps for ~7m -> errors start. They saw error bursts ~09:06:30. Customer contacted support at 09:10.
tim-customer: here are the error responses we get:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 30
}
X-RateLimit-Limit: 36000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Window: 60
```
We were told we have a '36k' quota which should be fine for our traffic. :confused:

maria-eng-runtime: thanks — sharing logs, looks odd. That X-RateLimit-Window: 60 suggests the runtime is interpreting quota as "per minute". If the tenant quota was intended as hourly units, that mismatch would cause aggressive throttling.

jordan-eng-sre: I can see pool-43 metrics in prometheus: sawtooth requests and KV-cache evictions around the spikes. Autoscaler events: no new nodes from 09:05-09:12 despite CPU jumping. There are two clues:
- autoscaler ignored scale-up because "burst_policy" flag was false for this pool
- per-tenant rate-limit gate tripped and started returning 429s, which bled into our routing backpressure and suppressed traffic signals to autoscale

alex-support: oof. Do we have the tenant config? Where was quota set?

maria-eng-runtime: fetching tenant config from vault (redacted):
```
tenant_id: tenant-43
quota:
  units: "36000"
  window: "60"  # units interpreted as seconds in runtime
  unit_type: "tokens"
```
The provisioning UI / billing team recorded that as "36k per hour" but the runtime reads window=60 (seconds). So effectively tenant got 36k/sec? no, effectively 36k per minute because window=60.

beth-account: That matches an event in our billing logs — the UI allowed a free-text "window" and the customer selected "60" while they meant 60 minutes. We need better validation.

leah-customer-success: Customer insists they requested hourly. They want a workaround now.

jordan-eng-sre: Quick mitigation options:
1) temporary quota override (internal admin) to raise window to 3600 for tenant-43
2) enable burst_policy for pool-43 so autoscaler will react to load despite some 429s
3) add a short-lived routing fallback to other compatible pools (will increase cost)

maria-eng-runtime: repro steps so eng can validate locally:
- set tenant quota to units=36000, window=60
- send a sustained load: `heygen -c 2000 -d 8s --header "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-key>" http://pool-43.internal/v1/generate`
- observe X-RateLimit-* and 429s in runtime logs
- check autoscaler metrics: no scale up if burst_policy=false

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed no recent runtime deploys to pool-43. Last config change: 1776498000 by beth-account.

alex-support: Can someone apply the temporary override? Customer is pretty upset.

maria-eng-runtime: I'll push the override now. Admin call:
```
POST /internal/admin/tenants/tenant-43/quota-override
body: { "units": "36000", "window": "3600", "reason": "emergency customer workaround" }
```
I will also flip burst_policy=true for pool-43 for 10m.

jordan-eng-sre: confirmed — after override we saw remaining >0 and 429s stopped ~09:16. Autoscaler started adding one node at 09:17 and latency dropped.

tim-customer: Thanks, saw errors clear and latency returned to normal. Appreciate the quick fix.

beth-account: We'll follow up with TimCorp billing to correct the UI confusion and offer a one-time credit. Also filing an internal UX bug: free-text window units.

leah-customer-success: next actions:
- eng-runtime to add stricter validation on quota window units (seconds/minutes/hours dropdown)
- eng-sre to add alert for "rate-limit suppression causing autoscale suppression" pattern
- account to correct tenant quota and confirm with customer
- support to update incident notes and close if customer OK

alex-support: leaving a note here for postmortem. tagging @maria-eng-runtime @jordan-eng-sre for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

maria-eng-runtime: Will open a short RFC to change the provisioning schema and add a migration check. ETA: PR by EOD.
jordan-eng-sre: I'll create an alert runbook and add a Grafana panel for detectability.

leah-customer-success: Customer confirmed resolution at 09:25 and will monitor. Closing loop once billing touchpoint done.

alex-support: thanks all. Closing this thread when billing confirms.
